Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

bioToolkit 1.2.1

Saving

  • save_plot() has a new family argument, default "Arial": the font of all text without a font of its own (a base.family set in the theme is kept). PDFs used cairo’s “sans” (Helvetica or a stand-in such as Nimbus Sans) while PNGs used the system’s sans-serif (Arial on Windows / Linux, Helvetica on macOS), so the two formats could differ. family = NULL keeps the devices’ defaults.
  • PNG, JPEG, TIFF and BMP files are now written with cairo (png(type = "cairo"), …) instead of ragg, so that PDF and raster files share one font, set with family. ragg is no longer in Suggests.

bioToolkit 1.2.0

DE plots

  • plot_fc_quadrant() (breaking changes):
    • New color.by. The default, "consistency", colours the features significant in both comparisons by direction: “Consistently up” (red), “Consistently down” (blue) and “Inconsistent” (opposite directions, yellow #DDAA33); all others are grey (“Others”). "direction" keeps only the consistent classes in colour, with counts in the top-right and bottom-left corners only. "significance" is the former five-class scheme (both same / both opposite / x only / y only / neither); categories now applies to it only. Coloured classes are drawn 1.4 times larger, and cols takes the class names of the chosen scheme (up, down, inconsistent, other for the first two).
    • padj.cutoff and logfc.cutoff are replaced with padj.cutoff.x, padj.cutoff.y, logfc.cutoff.x and logfc.cutoff.y. Fold change cutoffs above 0 are drawn as thin dashed grey lines at +-cutoff.
    • New trend.interval ("confidence", default; "prediction"; "none"): the 95% band around the trend line. The band is now drawn under the points, the line above them.

bioToolkit 1.1.2

Saving

  • save_plot(): the minus argument (new in 1.1.0) is removed. Negative numbers on axes and colour bars keep ggplot2’s hyphen (“-2”), as in PNGs, instead of the wider minus sign (U+2212).
  • PDFs are still written with cairo_pdf(), so a hyphen stays a hyphen, but with cairo’s default “sans” font, resolved by the system, rather than the font looked up with systemfonts (removed from Suggests).

bioToolkit 1.1.1

Change default volcano up and down colors to brighter ones.

bioToolkit 1.1.0

Saving

  • save_plot() writes PDFs with cairo_pdf() when R has cairo support. Base pdf() drew every hyphen with the wider minus glyph (its ISOLatin1 encoding on Linux / macOS), could not draw Unicode text and did not embed its fonts. The PDF’s default font is the one ragg uses for PNGs (found with systemfonts, new in Suggests), so PDF and PNG files of a plot use the same font and have nearly the same size. Without cairo, or with device given, ggsave()’s device is used as before.
  • New minus argument (default TRUE): negative numbers in the labels of continuous and binned scales (axes, colour bars) are written with a true minus sign (U+2212). Text typed in titles, labels or gene names is not changed.

bioToolkit 1.0.0

First stable release: plot revisions after the first round of the documentation website, scaled dimension arrows, a palette page.

Dimension arrows scale with the panel

  • DimPlot_bioToolkit(), FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(), DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(), format_sc_plots(), add_dimension_arrows(): the dimension arrows keep a fixed proportion to the panel. Their sizes are those of a 3.5-inch panel and are scaled with the panel’s shorter side when the plot is drawn: lengths, line width and label size. Small panels get small arrows that stay clear of the cells near the left and bottom edges (they used to run into them); large panels get larger arrows. New arrow.scale (default 1; in ... of the embedding plots) makes them larger or smaller at any size. The geometry arguments (arrow.length, text.font.size, …) are now sizes on a 3.5-inch panel. Plots without a fixed panel size (e.g. Seurat plots passed to format_sc_plots()) are scaled from the size they are drawn at.
  • The room left below and left of embedding panels for the arrow labels scales with the arrows (0.6 cm at 3.5 inches).

Group annotations: bars

Higher-level groups of rows or columns are drawn the same way in every plot: a bar along the group’s cells, 3.5 pt thick by default (group.bar.width), set a little off the grid, with the group’s name in bold beyond it. Bars are black by default, or coloured by group (*.cols, the same values as cols). By default they sit opposite the axis labels; *.side = "labels" moves them beyond the labels. New shared code in R/group_bars.R.

  • DotPlot_bioToolkit(): feature.group.cols, feature.group.side, split.by.cols, split.by.side, group.bar.width. Gene groups are now on top (right with flip = TRUE) with a bar instead of a thin bracket line; split.by blocks on the right (top when flipped) instead of the left.
  • VlnPlot_bioToolkit(): split.by.cols, split.by.side, group.bar.width; flipped split.by blocks are now on the right.
  • DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(): feature.group.cols, split.by.cols, group.bar.width (blocks of features opposite the feature names, blocks of columns on top).
  • plot_de_dots(): comparisons are marked by colour like the groups of the dot plot (comparison.marker = “dot” (default), “strip” or “none”; comparison.cols); groups and gene groups get bars (groups.cols, groups.side, feature.group.cols, feature.group.side, group.bar.width).
  • The dot-grid size legend (“% expressing”, “-log10 padj”) is black.

Changes

  • plot_multi_volcano(): the coloured band at 0 is replaced by a strip of fixed thickness above each comparison’s column with its name above it (comparison.cols, comparison.labels; formerly band.cols, band.labels, accepted with a deprecation warning), and dashed lines at the cutoffs. Non-significant genes are drawn in grey by default (show.ns = TRUE). groups get bars like split.by (groups.cols, groups.side). New flip lists the comparisons as rows (down left, up right; new cell.height, panel.width). Grouped comparisons are drawn together.
  • Diverging colour scales (dot plot z-scores, heatmaps, DE dots, enrichment grid NES, multi-volcano, density difference, diverging feature plots) keep their centre colour at 0 but are no longer forced symmetric: each end is the cutoff, or the data’s extreme on that side when closer, and each side is stretched to its own end (diverging_limits(), rescale_diverging()). Fixed logfc.limits given by the user are kept.
  • Legend titles are bold in every plot (theme_bioToolkit(), also plotmath titles); manipulate_sc_plot() / format_sc_plots() default to legend.title.bold = TRUE.
  • DimPlot_bioToolkit(), FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(), DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(), format_sc_plots(): new arrow.panels (“bottom.left” (default), “all”, “left”, “right”, “top”, “bottom”, “none”) sets which panels get the dimension arrows. In format_sc_plots() it replaces add.arrow and bottom.left.only (accepted with a deprecation warning), defaults to “bottom.left” (was every plot), and arrows a plot already has are replaced rather than added to.
  • VlnPlot_bioToolkit(): with a lowered y.max, violins and boxes are cut at the top of the axis (they ran past it) and points above it are not drawn.
  • plot_composition_scatter(): new error (“sem” (default), “sd” or “ci95”, t-based) for the per-sample error bars, now drawn with caps, 0.75 pt and black. The source data add x_sd, y_sd, x_error, y_error.
  • plot_fc_quadrant(): the x = 0 and y = 0 lines are 1 pt black; the correlation is bold, black and larger; new trend adds a least-squares line with its 95% confidence band.
  • plot_enrichment_dots(): strips of all panels have the same thickness, names centred; with several panels the legends are in two columns (colour bars, then size legends; new legend.layout, “stacked” for the previous single column); one panel shows its two legends side by side.
  • plot_gsea_rank(): NES and FDR bold and larger; the gene set ID is the second line of the title and the comparison a bold italic subtitle; new label / label.n / label.features name the leading-edge (or chosen) genes with an arrow to their ticks; new band = "none"; new italic.genes. The source data add leading_edge and labelled.
  • ggplotColours() is renamed ggplot_colors() (showColor -> show.colors); the old name still works, with a deprecation warning.
  • plot_multi_volcano(): with layout = "sina", non-significant genes are spread uniformly over the column, a grey block centred on 0, instead of forming a third shape between the cutoffs; up- and down-regulated genes keep their own shapes. With layout = "pvalue" (suited to bulk data), each side of 0 is scaled as a whole, so grey genes sit at their own significance. Non-significant genes are a lighter grey (“grey88”; plot_volcano() keeps “grey75”) and always drawn under the significant ones.
  • plot_gsea_rank(): leading-edge gene names at the small text size (9 pt, 8 pt when they need more than two lines; were 11 / 9 pt).
  • show_palettes() also draws your own colours: a vector of colours, or a list of palette names and colour vectors (one row each, labelled by the list’s names). Its first argument is renamed palettes (names still works, with a deprecation warning).

Documentation website

  • New “Colour palettes” page: every palette with the index and hex code of each colour, its type and source, and the plots that use it by default.
  • A custom “page not found” page (.github/404.md).
  • Home page: a general description of the package; plot conventions moved to the conventions table.
  • Figure essentials: theme tabs fixed and self-contained, panel versus cell sizes explained with examples, more legend extraction examples.
  • Guides show the new arguments; their code follows the new code style (one ggplot layer per line, one argument per line for long calls; see CONTRIBUTING.md).

bioToolkit 0.10.0

Package clean-up ahead of the documentation website (https://j-y26.github.io/bioToolkit/).

Removed

  • Legacy functions no longer maintained: peak_category_qc(), peak_category_plot(), peak_tss_enrichment(), peak_width_distribution(), peak_calc_frip(), peak_plot_frip(), grouped_bar_plot(), calc_module_scores() and calc_module_scores_ssgsea(). Their Suggests (ChIPseeker, GenomicRanges, IRanges, Rsamtools, rtracklayer, GSVA, BiocParallel, Biobase) and the unused aplot, data.table and stringr were dropped. format_gene_sets() is kept (now in R/gene_sets.R).

Deprecated argument names

The remaining older functions now use the package’s dot.case argument names. The old names are still accepted, with a deprecation warning (class deprecatedWarning), and positional calls are unchanged:

  • format_sc_plots(), manipulate_sc_plot(), add_dimension_arrows(): snake_case to dot.case (remove_axes -> remove.axes, arrow_length -> arrow.length, legend_position -> legend.position, …), and byrow -> by.row as in DimPlot_bioToolkit().
  • filter_de_genes(), rank_de_genes(), generate_de_rank_file(): de_results -> data, de_method -> method, pvalue_col -> padj.col, log2fc_col -> logfc.col, log2fc_min -> logfc.cutoff, pvalue_max -> padj.cutoff, save_file -> file, as in standardize_de() and plot_volcano().

Changes

  • filter_de_genes(), rank_de_genes(), generate_de_rank_file(): method now defaults to “auto” and also reads limma and Seurat tables (the columns come from the presets of standardize_de()); the method name ignores case as before. filter_de_genes() no longer returns all-NA rows for genes with an NA adjusted p-value.
  • format_sc_plots() keeps the relative widths and heights of a patchwork (they were passed to wrap_plots() under the wrong names and lost).
  • DimPlot_bioToolkit(), FeaturePlot_bioToolkit() and DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit() take the dot.case arrow arguments of add_dimension_arrows() in ... (e.g. arrow.length); the snake_case ones are deprecated.
  • format_gene_sets(to = "gmt") returns the GMT lines (it printed them and returned NULL); new file argument to write them. A gene listed twice in a set (e.g. from msigdbr) is kept once instead of failing.

Fixes found while writing the website guides

  • plot_multi_volcano() with groups: the comparison names under the grouped panels were dropped (out of the y range); they are drawn again.
  • plot_enrichment_dots(): the legends of stacked panels overlapped the next panel’s; legends are now collected into one column on the right. Panels side by side with different numbers of gene sets had names misaligned with their dots; they now have the same height (empty rows at the bottom of shorter panels). Long panel names are wrapped to fit their strip.
  • plot_composition_scatter(): groups with no cells in a panel of facet.by (or among cells) are no longer drawn and labelled at the origin.

Website

  • Documentation website with guides by task, run on public data (Kang et al. 2018 PBMCs; Alasoo et al. 2018 macrophages; MSigDB Hallmark), and the function index in 9 categories. Built by GitHub Actions when the version changes. Website files are excluded from the package build, and the packages needed only by the guides are in Config/Needs/website.

bioToolkit 0.9.0

Phase E of the visualization overhaul: bulk plots (B1, B2, B4, B5). The planned sample-to-sample heatmap (B3) was dropped; use corrplot or ComplexHeatmap.

New

  • plot_ma(): MA plot (log2 fold change against mean expression) with the classes, colours, labels and arguments of plot_volcano(). Mean expression as the DE tool reports it: log2 values (edgeR logCPM, limma AveExpr) as they are, linear ones (DESeq2 baseMean) on a log10 axis (mean.scale); optional robust trend line (trend, lowess); counts of up / down features in the right corners. Shrunken fold changes (DESeq2 lfcShrink()) are the recommended input (logfc.col).
  • plot_pca(): PCA score plot of samples from a prcomp result or a normalized matrix (top n.top = 500 most variable features), coloured (discrete or continuous), shaped and labelled by sample covariates, % of variance in the axis titles, optional ellipses (groups of at least 4 samples) and scree panel; warns on raw counts; square panel; scores and covariates as source data.
  • plot_variance_explained(): variance explained by sample covariates. View “genes”: per-gene fractions as violins (ordered by median, Residuals last), or stacked bars for selected features; read from a variancePartition result, or computed with linear models (R-squared split between covariates by the LMG method, so fractions sum to 1 and do not depend on the order of the covariates). View “pcs”: R-squared of each top PC on each covariate as tiles, under bars of each PC’s % variance.
  • plot_fc_quadrant(): log2 fold change in one comparison against another (two time points, two tissues, RNA vs ATAC / ChIP), coloured by where each feature is significant (both, same or opposite direction; one only; neither), with counts per quadrant, the Spearman (or Pearson) correlation, a y = x diagonal and labels of the top features per quadrant. The two tables may come from different tools; peaks are mapped to genes with map.y (one peak per gene: the most significant by default).

Internal

  • plot_volcano() uses the shared check_de_cutoffs() and the new de_direction(), also used by plot_ma() and plot_fc_quadrant(). Output unchanged.

bioToolkit 0.8.0

Phase D of the visualization overhaul: single-cell plots (S1-S4).

Breaking changes

  • group.by / split.by now mean the same in every plot (user decision 2026-10-13): group.by is the lower-level grouping whose levels are compared, marked by their colours; split.by is the higher-level grouping, drawn like facets (labelled blocks or panels). DotPlot_bioToolkit() follows it: with split.by, rows are blocks of split.by (named on the left), each with one row per group.by level marked by its colour. What was DotPlot_bioToolkit(group.by = "cell_type", split.by = "condition") is now DotPlot_bioToolkit(group.by = "condition", split.by = "cell_type") (and the dots show the condition colours). This is the opposite of Seurat::DotPlot() / VlnPlot()’s split.by, and matches the panels of DimPlot_bioToolkit() / FeaturePlot_bioToolkit().
  • plot_meta_scatter() is removed; use plot_composition_scatter().
  • summarize_group_meta(): cells.use is now cells; group.by is a single column; new facet.by and sample.by; the result has columns facet, sample (when given), condition, group, count, total and prop (was total_count_condition). It no longer calls gc().

New

  • VlnPlot_bioToolkit(): per-cell violins with a box (quartiles and median) and a random sample of cells as rasterized points, for genes, metadata (QC metrics, module scores) or both, from a Seurat object or a data frame. One panel (and value axis) per feature: log and percent take TRUE or feature names; y.max zooms to a number or a quantile (“q99”) without dropping cells; zeros = "exclude" / "annotate" for sparse genes (violins of the cells above 0, with the % above 0); flip (horizontal), stack (thin rows sharing the group axis); split.by as labelled blocks of violins; fixed violin sizes; source data per cell with the assay and layer.
  • RidgePlot_bioToolkit(): density ridges with the same data arguments (needs ggridges, now in Suggests); overlap sets the ridge height; one bandwidth per feature.
  • DoHeatmap_bioToolkit(): heatmap of genes x cells (columns = "cells", at most max.cells per group, seeded) or group means (columns = "groups"), z-scored per gene from the “data” layer by default (across all plotted cells, before downsampling, or across the columns), so that any gene can be drawn (Seurat’s “scale.data” holds only variable genes). Columns in blocks of split.by (named, with gaps) and groups compared within them, marked by a coloured dot (default) or strip with a legend; gene blocks from a named list (e.g. top_markers()); extra annotation strips (annotations); gene names drawn when rows are tall enough, on the right or left (label.side), or a few named with leader lines (label.features). No clustering (use ComplexHeatmap).
  • plot_composition_scatter(): proportion (or count) of each group in one condition against another, with the y = x line: split.by with levels x and y on the axes, facet.by panels (proportions within each), optional per-sample proportions with mean +- SEM (sample.by; pooled by default), log axes, fold.lines, labels for all or selected groups; square panels with the same range on both axes.
  • DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(): where on an embedding the cells of a condition are enriched or depleted relative to a reference. One kernel density per condition (one bandwidth for all), normalized to sum to 1 so that cell numbers do not matter; optionally one density per sample, averaged per condition (sample.by); measure = "difference" (relative to the reference’s peak) or "log2ratio"; sparse regions masked; cells coloured by the value at their position (draw = "cells") or the grid as a raster; one panel per compared condition, one symmetric diverging scale; optional density contours, group labels and dimension arrows.
  • Palette “teal-yellow” (teal - black - yellow, built as Seurat’s PurpleAndYellow), the default of DoHeatmap_bioToolkit() for z-scores of cells; heatmaps of group means default to “blue-magenta” (light centre).
  • Genomic regions (e.g. peaks “chr1-100-200”) are no longer set in italics as gene names.
  • Internal: the kernel smoothing of FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(geom = "density") is split into kde_grid() and grid_interpolate(), shared with DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit() (results unchanged).

bioToolkit 0.7.0

Phase C of the visualization overhaul: the dot-grid family and DE summaries.

New

  • DotPlot_bioToolkit(): marker dot plot (% of cells expressing = dot area, mean expression = colour), covering Seurat::DotPlot() and SCpubr::do_DotPlot(): scale (z-scored means, default TRUE), average = "linear" (Seurat: log1p(mean(expm1(x)))) or "log" (SCpubr: mean(x)), gene groups from a named list (labelled brackets), split.by (rows of a group kept together), clustering of genes and groups, flip, pct.min (SCpubr’s dot.min) and pct.max. New: group markers in the groups’ DimPlot_bioToolkit() colours (group.marker: a coloured dot by default, a colour strip, or none), unscaled means on “viridis_r” (yellow = low), gene names in italics, dot areas on a fixed 0-100% scale (comparable between figures), fixed cell sizes, and source data with the assay and layer used.
  • Dot-grid plots (DotPlot_bioToolkit(), plot_de_dots(), plot_enrichment_grid()) have 1 pt x and y axes on the dots, with the group markers outside the axes and no grid lines through them; theme_bioToolkit("grid") has the same 1 pt axes.
  • top_markers(): top marker genes per group from FindAllMarkers() output, as the named list DotPlot_bioToolkit() takes.
  • plot_de_dots(): genes x comparisons, colour = log2 fold change, size = -log10 adjusted p-value; non-significant results faded, significant ones ringed, in a “Significance” legend that spells out both cutoffs (significance = "fade", or “grey” / “hide”); reads edgeR, DESeq2, limma and Seurat results through standardize_de(); gene groups, comparison groups and clustering. Replaces de_dot_plot().
  • plot_multi_volcano(): all DE genes of many comparisons, one column each, with a band at +-logfc.cutoff, counts of up / down genes, labels of the top genes per column; points spread by density (layout = "sina"), by p-value or at random; coloured by significance, direction or the number of comparisons sharing the gene; optional groups of comparisons.
  • standardize_enrichment(): reads fgsea, clusterProfiler (GSEA and over-representation, objects or tables) and GSEA desktop results into one table; MSigDB names made readable (“TNFA signaling via NFKB”), GO descriptions capitalised (“Extracellular matrix organization”).
  • plot_enrichment_dots(): the top gene sets of one result, or of several (one panel each, e.g. up- and down-regulated genes, from a named list): gene ratio (or NES) on x, size = count, colour = -log10 padj. Each panel has its own single-hue palette and a tinted strip; panels stacked (shared x-axis), side by side or in a grid; shared colour / size limits by default; legends always in the same order (colour bar, then size); term.replace to shorten names. GSEA counts and ratios come from the leading edge.
  • plot_enrichment_grid(): gene sets x comparisons (NES or -log10 padj), non-significant results faded.
  • plot_enrichment_bars(): diverging NES bar chart of one comparison, names opposite their bars; faded (non-significant) bars explained in a legend.
  • plot_gsea_rank(): running enrichment score, gene positions over a band coloured by the ranking metric, and the ranked metric (grey; show.metric = FALSE drops it) of one gene set, with NES and FDR; compact, touching panels. Takes a clusterProfiler gseaResult, or fgsea results with the ranked list and gene sets. The score is computed in the package and checked against the reported one.
  • Palettes: single-hue sequential “seq-purple”, “seq-blue”, “seq-teal”, “seq-green”, “seq-orange”, “seq-red”, “seq-magenta” (from grDevices::hcl.colors(), trimmed to the same lightness range). Any palette name with “_r” appended is that palette reversed (“viridis_r”, “npg_r”, “seq-blue_r”, and RColorBrewer names such as “BuPu_r”); reversed palettes are not stored.

Changed

  • The sequential palette “bioToolkit” is removed: it was viridisLite’s plasma reversed (and trimmed at its pale end). FeaturePlot_bioToolkit() now defaults to “plasma_r”, plasma exactly reversed, so its lowest values are plasma’s pale yellow (#F0F921) rather than the golden yellow the trimmed version ended on.

  • FeaturePlot_bioToolkit() gains assay: genes are read from that assay only (the default assay when NULL, as before), the assay and layer are reported in a message and written to the source data, and a gene that is only in another assay is an error instead of being read from it silently.

  • save_plot(): a legend taller (or wider) than its panel no longer adds blank space around single plots. The file is enlarged only as far as the legend actually spills beyond the plot (as already done for patchworks). Files of plots whose legend fits are unchanged.

  • fetch_features() and feature_is_gene() moved to R/seurat_data.R, with the new assay helpers.

  • DOSE added to Suggests (reading clusterProfiler result objects).

Removed

  • de_dot_plot(): use plot_de_dots(). Its arguments map as de_results -> de (with comparison.col), feature_var -> feature.col, logFC_var -> logfc.col, p_val_var -> padj.col, logFC_cutoff / p_val_cutoff -> logfc.cutoff / padj.cutoff, invert -> flip, sig_only = TRUE -> significance = "hide", group_by_features -> features as a named list, group_by_comparisons -> groups, colours -> cols.

bioToolkit 0.6.0

Phase B of the visualization overhaul: fixes and removals.

New

  • extract_legend(): takes the legend out of a plot, to save it as its own file with save_plot() (sized to fit, with the fonts of the output format) or place it in a layout. By default the legend is exactly as in the plot; direction, title.position and any legend.* theme setting change it. Hidden legends (legend.position = "none") can be extracted too.
  • save_plot() accepts legends from extract_legend().

Removed

  • annotation_sankey_plot(). Annotation concordance is better shown as a contingency heatmap (e.g. with ComplexHeatmap). plotly is no longer suggested.
  • plot_top_pca_loadings(). extract_pc_loadings() stays; a PCA score plot (plot_pca()) is planned.
  • plot_volcano2(): merged into plot_volcano() (annotate.counts = "arrow").

Changed

  • The sequential palette “bioToolkit” is removed: it was viridisLite’s plasma reversed (and trimmed at its pale end). FeaturePlot_bioToolkit() now defaults to “plasma_r”, plasma exactly reversed, so its lowest values are plasma’s pale yellow (#F0F921) rather than the golden yellow the trimmed version ended on.

  • plot_volcano() is rewritten (breaking change: new arguments):

    • reads edgeR, DESeq2, limma and Seurat results through standardize_de() (method, feature.col, logfc.col, p.col, padj.col replace de_method, x, y, label);
    • the y-axis is the -log10 adjusted p-value, the same value that decides significance (padj.cutoff, logfc.cutoff replace p_cutoff, fc_cutoff);
    • labels are chosen explicitly with label = "top" (the label.n most significant per direction, plus any label.features), "selected" (only label.features) or "none". The old behaviour of silently replacing requested genes with the top 10 per direction is gone, and labels are no longer dropped when crowded. Labels are bold, and italic for genes (italic.genes);
    • annotate.counts = "corner" (old plot_volcano()), "arrow" (old plot_volcano2()) or "none";
    • fixed panel size (panel.width, panel.height; square by default: panel.height = panel.width, so panel.width alone resizes the plot), theme_bioToolkit(), transparent background; points are rasterized above 5,000 features (raster, raster.dpi = 1000), labels and text stay vector;
    • non-significant points are drawn first, so they never hide DE points;
    • p-values of 0 no longer stretch the axis to 1e-300;
    • cols = c(up = , down = , ns = ) replaces up_color, down_color, non_de_color; up.label, down.label, ns.label replace up_label, down_label, non_de_label. Text sizes follow the theme.

  • de_dot_plot() fixes: non-significant dots are now grey (nsig_color, default "grey70" as documented); logFC values beyond col_limits_logFC take the colour of the nearest limit instead of the non-significant grey; the default colour limits are symmetric and computed from the plotted significant dots (col_limits_logFC = NULL); p-values of 0 no longer give infinite dot sizes; features are matched case-sensitively (gene-symbol case differs between species); the size legend names the p-value column; the group strips of the inverted plot follow x_group_label_position; the “removed due to non-significance” warning only appears with sig_only = TRUE.

  • calc_expr_corr(): its volcano works again (it passed a vector as label), is saved at the volcano’s own fixed size, and base_dir is created even when plot_model = FALSE. Default dpi is now 1000.

  • Theme size presets are removed: the “nature”, “cell” and “slides” presets, the option bioToolkit.preset and the preset argument of theme_bioToolkit(). One set of sizes applies everywhere: 11 pt text (9 pt tick labels and legend text, 12 pt titles and strips), 1 pt axis lines and ticks (were 0.5 pt), 0.5 pt other lines. theme_bioToolkit(base.size = ) still scales the text.

  • DimPlot_bioToolkit() (label.size, legend.pt.size) and FeaturePlot_bioToolkit() (label.size, legend.length, legend.width) show their defaults again (3.5, 3.5; 3.5, 1.5, 0.15) instead of NULL; the plots are unchanged.

  • Function signatures list one argument per line (no change in behaviour).

bioToolkit 0.5.0

Phase A of the visualization overhaul: the foundations every plot builds on.

New

  • theme_bioToolkit(): one theme for all plots, in three layouts (“axis”, “grid”, “embedding”), with size presets for the printed figure (“default”, “nature”, “cell”, “slides”). options(bioToolkit.preset = "nature") switches every plot of the package at once.
  • italic_labels(): gene names in italics as scale labels.
  • panel_size_theme(): fixed panel sizes in inches for any ggplot.
  • save_plot(): saves a plot to a file sized to fit it (replaces save_dimplot()); also saves plots without fixed panels at a given width and height.
  • Palettes: bt_palette() returns the colours of a palette as a plain hex vector, to pick, reorder and name by index (bt_palette("scanpy-20")[c(1, 3, 2)]); show_palettes() shows each colour with its index; list_palettes() lists names, types and sources; check_palette() flags colours that are hard to tell apart with colour vision deficiency. Ships the scanpy palettes, colour-blind safe palettes (Okabe-Ito, Paul Tol), journal styles (NPG, AAAS, NEJM, Lancet, JAMA, JCO), viridis and Tol sequential palettes, and diverging palettes.
  • standardize_de(): reads edgeR, DESeq2, limma and Seurat results (or a list of them, one per comparison) into standard columns.
  • export_source_data(): writes the data behind a plot, or each plot of a patchwork, to CSV or XLSX.

Changed

  • The sequential palette “bioToolkit” is removed: it was viridisLite’s plasma reversed (and trimmed at its pale end). FeaturePlot_bioToolkit() now defaults to “plasma_r”, plasma exactly reversed, so its lowest values are plasma’s pale yellow (#F0F921) rather than the golden yellow the trimmed version ended on.

  • Plots have a transparent background by default (bg = "transparent"), so that they can be placed on any background; use bg = "white" for an opaque one. save_plot() keeps it in PDF, PNG, TIFF and SVG, including for patchworks, and uses white for JPEG and BMP.

  • The default colours of groups are now “scanpy-20” for up to 20 groups and “scanpy-102” beyond (before: the ggplot2 hue palette). Every level of a grouping variable gets a colour, including levels with no plotted cell, so that a plot of a subset is coloured like a plot of the whole object.

  • cols of DimPlot_bioToolkit() accepts palette names; cols of FeaturePlot_bioToolkit() accepts palette names or colours from low to high (c(low, high), c(low, mid, high)). Colours given as a function and the viridis letters “A” to “H” are no longer accepted.

  • DimPlot_bioToolkit() and FeaturePlot_bioToolkit() take their text sizes, legend keys, colour bar and arrows from the theme preset: legend.text.size, strip.text.size, label.size, legend.pt.size, legend.length and legend.width now default to NULL (from the preset). At the default preset the plots are unchanged.

  • grouped_bar_plot() and peak_plot_frip() take their colours from the package palettes instead of Seurat (default "polychrome-36", the same colours as Seurat’s “polychrome”); Seurat’s “glasbey”, “stepped” and “parade” are no longer available.

  • calc_expr_corr() saves its volcano plot with save_plot().

  • Requires R >= 4.1.0.

Removed

  • save_dimplot() (renamed save_plot()) and its deprecated alias save_umap().

Dependencies

  • Suggests: writexl (XLSX export); png and jpeg (tests only).
